summary: Spec fidelity + mutation probe (checker.md L2.input-dash-values: 'accepted as values (no option, file or inline-JSON misreading)'; spec 11.9): read_as_value (input.rs) counts ANY refusal whose field names the argument or /operands and whose error.received equals the value as 'read as a value', whatever the code. A tool that reads a document value {x, [x or -x as inline JSON or an option and refuses it as INPUT_INVALID, reason INVALID_VALUE, field /operands/0, received <the value> passes the MUST row. Probe: a wrapper over the conforming L2 fake answering exactly that for those three values: with received set, L2.input-dash-values pass and atip check exits 0 (level met); the control with received left out fails L2.input-dash-values only (plus L0.no-null for the null the wrapper printed). The ruling's own cases are domain and precondition refusals of a value that was read as a value; an INPUT_* code means the document was rejected, which is the misreading itself. Blast radius: every tool at L2; the seeded case dashValuesAsOptions refuses with USAGE and no received, so atip.checkl2input.13 cannot see it. Fix: accept a refusal as a value only when its code is not INPUT_INVALID/INPUT_CONFLICT/INPUT_TOO_LARGE (or the reason is not framing) and the value is quoted as received; keep the precondition fall-through.
